newsitem.title: UK: BAA sees windfall tax hit 70 to 100 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: BAA sees windfall tax hit 70 to 100 mln stg.

text.p: UK airports operator BAA Plc told Reuters on Wednesday that an initial assessment of its windfall tax exposure put the levy at between 70 million and 100 million stg.
A spokesman for the group told Reuters BAA would have to borrow to pay for the tax, bearing in mind its rolling capital expenditure programme.
He added there would be an effect on its gearing levels, which currently stand at 33.3 percent, but would not elaborate on the effect.
"We'll have to borrow to pay for this and that will have
a small effect on our gearing," said the BAA spokesman.
He said the group would have to borrow more because it was locked in a 10-year 4.4 billion stg investment programme, rolling out 500 million of investment per annum.
BAA does not intend to mount a legal challenge to the tax.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown detailed the windfall tax on privatised utilities in his first budget since Labour took power in May.
